message.content: {"caption":"Pass@k results across five scaling factors, comparing one bar series with two line series.","description":"A line-and-bar chart plots Pass@k (vertical axis, with ticks at 36, 45, 54, 63, and 72) against scaling factor k (horizontal axis, 1 through 5). The vertical axis begins at 36 rather than zero. The legend identifies gray bars as “MaTTS w/o memory,” the blue line with diamond markers as “MaTTS w/o aggregation,” and the blue line with triangle markers as “MaTTS.” Values are printed beside the marks. For k=1 through 5, the gray-bar values are 39.0, 47.6, 49.7, 51.3, and 52.4; the diamond-series values are 49.7, 50.8, 52.9, 55.1, and 56.1; and the triangle-series values are 49.7, 51.3, 54.5, 58.8, and 62.1. All three series rise as k increases. The triangle series ties the diamond series at 49.7 for k=1, then is higher at each subsequent factor and rises most strongly. The diamond series also increases, while remaining below the triangle series from k=2 onward.
